column1: # Which scaffold a page's blocks are compiled with. One row per page.
# `unit`    a file under scaffold/units/, compiled alongside every block of
#           that page, supplying identifiers the page names but no block
# `prelude` a file under scaffold/preludes/, which REPLACES the generic wrapper
#           for that page's blocks -- a typed handler class, say, so that a
#           block which is the body of a method has the method to sit in.
#           `-` for none. THERE ARE NONE, since 016 phase 5: the four carried
#           from 015's harness were mapped to no page and declared domain
#           types, so they were deleted. A prelude obeys the unit rule below.
# THE UNIT OF ADMISSION IS A PAGE, NOT A BLOCK. A page's blocks share a world,
# which is what makes the hand-work tractable and what stops a scaffold being
# tuned until one stubborn block goes green.
# THE UNIT RULE. A unit supplies what its pages' blocks name and nothing else,
# typed from a pinned package or the BCL -- never `dynamic`. For a unit mapped
# to pages P, `--report` checks, and a violation is a finding:
#   1. every type it declares is named by a BUILT block on P. A stub for a
#      type a page names and never shows is allowed (spec 017 P0-3); a type
#      the page tells the reader to write is not. That second half is a
#      judgement, checked by reading what `--list-scaffold` prints, not here
#   2. no block on P declares a type of that name -- a stub must never stand
#      in for a type the page itself declares in another block
#   3. every member it declares -- field, property, method -- is named by a
#      BUILT block on P, so a stub carries only what the page calls
#   4. it declares no `global using`. A missing `using` is the page's to
#      repair, where the reader sees it; a unit never supplies a namespace
# The static class a unit's own `// blockcheck: using static X;` line brings
# into scope is exempt from 1, since no block names it; its members are not
# exempt from 3. A page is listed here only if its unit makes at least one
# block build. `baseline.tsv` records the scaffold each admitted block was
